correctness.rationale: Exact geometric barycentric orbit model; orbit matching iff projections define a G-equivariant bijection of transitive G-orbits; normalizer index is its cardinality; pairwise disjointness precisely the multigraph matching rule; independent orbit types form simplicial joins. The regular five-copy case has an actual simplicial retraction to the ordinary five-by-five chessboard; ordinary H_2=Z/3 is explicitly cited. Eight small actions tested via all eligible-edge-orbit subsets, and parallel-edge face counts and retraction exhaustively tested for 19,091 board matchings. Boundary cases (trivial G, no compatible stabilizer types, fixed row/column orbits) are included by proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A diagonal G-action on both shores forces each eligible edge orbit to encode a G-equivariant bijection of transitive orbits. That is a different admissibility condition from one-shore column permutations or weighted-capacity multiple chessboards. For a single orbit on each shore the formula reduces to the known discrete centralizer theorem; for multiple orbit copies, disjoint orbit pairs coexist and yield nontrivial joins, which that theorem does not classify.

originality.rationale: The complete geometric fixed-complex classification by row/column transitive G-set types and normalizer-quotient parallel-edge multiplicities is not stated or implied by inspected classical ordinary matching homology sources or by the indexed separately-transitive special case. Transitive rows/columns give only a discrete set, while general actions yield joins and positive-dimensional homology, including a split 3-torsion example. Novelty is an assessment against accessible sources, not independence or definitive priority.
residual_risks: A non-indexed equivalent description of two-shore equivariant orbit-matchings may exist in group-complex or coset-complex literature.

Even though the theorem extends an inspected transitive special case, independent mathematical and publication-priority review could identify a stronger prior result.

value.rationale: The structural all-group fixed-space PL decomposition is a natural classification determined by subgroup conjugacy classes, normalizer quotients, and finite orbit multiplicities; it reveals non-discrete joins for nontransitive actions, and supplies a uniform family of genuine geometric fixed spaces with a split nonzero integral 3-torsion group. Arbitrary finite G-sets and nonabelian examples qualify beyond a single parameter table; the classical base torsion is not part of the new contribution.
